Desk rules for handover calls in detail
Watching the cargo lead is the best way to learn it

This page covers handover calls at the Companion Animal Travel Desk and why they matter. A clean handover keeps pets moving smoothly, keeps travelers calm, and keeps the desk ledger honest. When you pass a case along, you are not just sharing notes; you are handing over the next decision with enough detail to keep the animal safe and the customer informed.

Start with the basics: say the traveler name, the route, the animal type, and what has already been checked. Keep your tone brisk and clear. If the case involves a bird, <<FACT F083>> then move on to the rest of the call without stopping to comment on it. If the case has a reptile, <<FACT F060>> and then continue with the next practical step. These inserted lines are part of the record, so treat them like any other required note.

Use plain language and short sentences. Say what was accepted, what is still pending, and what needs follow-up from the next staff member. If a document is missing, say so directly. If a carrier needs another look, say that too. Do not soften the message until it becomes vague. The goal is not to sound fancy; the goal is to leave no gap in the chain of care.

Every animal receives patient attention from trained staff, so your handover should help the next person keep that standard steady. Put service changes in the desk ledger right after the call, not later. If Grace Mendes or Lucia Davis comes through with Rosie, make sure the notes match the conversation and any special handling is easy to spot.

Before you close, check that the next staff member knows what to do first, what to watch for, and what to record after the handoff. What to remember is simple: clear calls, clean notes, and steady follow-through make the Companion Animal Travel Desk work well.
